problems.description: Session 1 deletes the entire baseline index.ts (Express Todo API seed, 'designed as a baseline for multi-session stories') and replaces it with a greenfield static-site-generator instead of building within or preserving the provided seams, destroying the intended multi-session baseline.

All SSG logic — markdown parsing, HTML escaping, page/index document templates — is collapsed into a single monolithic generator.ts with no layer separation, regressing from the seed's explicit models/routes/error-handling structure.
package.json configures jest + ts-jest but the commit adds no test files; the new generator/cli code ships with zero coverage.
SonarQube reports 42 convention violations and a 0.52 convention score (smells +2, cognitive complexity +31); the generator.ts/parser code does not meet the repo's naming-convention bar.
escapeHtml reconstructs its HTML-entity lookup object inside the regex callback on every matched character instead of hoisting it to a module-level constant.

Discrepancy: the shown code uses camelCase functions and PascalCase interfaces (Page, BuildOptions), yet listed violations claim snake_case functions and PascalCase classes — those may target truncated config.ts, which I could not verify from the visible diff.

strengths: Proper ESM TypeScript scaffolding with separate build (tsc) and test (jest) scripts and pinned devDependencies
Typed public interfaces (Page, BuildOptions) and defensive type guards (toTags, toDateString) handle arbitrary front-matter values safely
CLI errors surface to stderr with a non-zero exit code and a clear usage message
commit_reviews.summary: The agent greenfield-replaced the provided multi-session baseline with a monolithic, untested static-site-generator scaffold, earning a poor architectural-fit score (0.4) — it discards existing patterns wholesale and ships above the convention bar (0.52 measured) — while the raw output is competent, modern TypeScript.

problems.description: Handlebars partials are registered on the module-global Handlebars object via loadPartials, so partial state persists across buildSite invocations (fine for a one-shot CLI, but a leak if buildSite is ever called repeatedly in-process).

renderPage reuses renderTemplate by passing path.join(templatesDir, 'layouts') as the 'templatesDir' argument, overloading the function's contract to render the layout; clearer to render the layout as a distinct second call or pass an explicit path.
Handlebars.compile is invoked per page inside renderTemplate; templates/layouts could be compiled once and cached per build.
SonarQube reports cognitive complexity +19 for this feature size; the branching in parseArguments and the layered render/layout flow add complexity that could be simplified.

strengths: Feature is additive and backward-compatible: existing markdown->HTML output via pageDocument is preserved when no templates dir exists.
Respects existing module boundaries: arg parsing stays in cli.ts, build logic in generator.ts, matching the established structure.
Solid test coverage added for templates, layouts, and partials integration.
toTemplateName guards against path traversal (rejecting '/', '\', '.', '..'), good security hygiene for a user-supplied template name.
commit_reviews.summary: A clean, backward-compatible templating feature that fits the existing SSG architecture and patterns, with minor global-state and compile-per-page smells. NOTE: the 0.52 convention score and listed violations (PascalCase/UPPER_CASE/snake_case) are pre-existing codebase style choices flagged by the analyzer, not introduced by this commit; the new code consistently follows the existing snake_case/camelCase conventions, so the measured score understates this commit's actual convention adherence.

problems.description: Async request handler in serveSite awaits decodeURIComponent/readFile/fileExists with no try/catch, so a malformed URL (decodeURIComponent throws) or I/O error rejects the promise with no handler — unhandled rejection can crash or leave the request hanging.

Cognitive complexity +52 (SonarQube); the rebuild-queue flag logic (rebuilding/rebuildQueued recursion) and the nested serveSite lifecycle add complexity that could be factored into a small state machine or class.
contentType() only maps html/css/js/json/svg and defaults everything else to octet-stream, so png/jpg/ico fonts served from dist get the wrong MIME type.
tests/server.test.ts (29 lines) covers basic serving but not the live-reload injection, WebSocket broadcast, or rebuild-on-chokidar-event paths — the highest-risk logic is untested.
reloadScript is declared camelCase while the surrounding module-style convention (and the analyzer's 'Constants should be UPPER_CASE') favors LIVE_RELOAD_SCRIPT-style uppercase constants.

strengths: Reuses buildSite for the initial build and rebuilds instead of duplicating the generator pipeline — clean composition with the existing module.
Rebuild debouncing (rebuilding/rebuildQueued) prevents overlapping rebuilds on rapid chokidar bursts.
Path traversal guard (outputDir prefix check) on file serving is a sound security default.
CLI integration is consistent: parseArguments extended for --port with integer/range validation, usage string updated.
New server module ships with a test file and typed interfaces (ServeOptions, DevelopmentServer).
commit_reviews.summary: A solid, well-composed integration of a dev server that reuses the existing generator pipeline with proper rebuild debouncing and a traversal guard, but it carries some debt in unhandled async request errors, incomplete MIME coverage, and an untested live-reload path. Flag: mechanical convention score 0.52 (42 violations incl. 'Classes should use PascalCase' in cli.ts/config.ts, where no classes exist and config.ts is absent) appears to be analyzer noise and contradicts the diff's observable TS/ESM conventions; the measured score understates real adherence.

problems.description: The hook dispatcher in SsgEngine.run() relies on non-null assertion (page!) and type casts (as NonNullable<Plugin['onFile']>) to force a uniform hook signature, which weakens type safety and will be brittle as hooks diverge.

tsx (an esbuild-based loader) is added as a runtime dependency solely to evaluate ssg.config.ts; it is a heavyweight dependency for config loading and may be better gated or replaced with a lighter runtime.
Mechanical convention score is 0.52 with 42 violations (PascalCase classes/interfaces, UPPER_CASE constants, snake_case functions) reported across cli.ts, config.ts, and generator.ts.
Refactor of the core build pipeline (extraction into plugins, new config loader) ships without visible accompanying tests in the diff; the plugin lifecycle hooks deserve coverage.
SonarQube reports cognitive complexity +15 and +1 smell in the refactored logic, concentrated in the new dispatch/config-loading code paths.

strengths: Introduces a clean plugin architecture: SsgEngine orchestrator with a well-defined hook lifecycle (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) decoupled from MarkdownPlugin and TemplatePlugin.
User-extensible via ssg.config.ts with type-safe TS config loading, so features can be added without modifying the core generator.
Net reduction of ~250 lines (342 added vs 247 removed) breaking down a monolithic generator into focused modules (config.ts, plugin types, plugins/).
Modern ESM conventions maintained: node: prefixed imports, .js extension specifiers, pathToFileURL usage for dynamic import.
commit_reviews.summary: Architecturally strong refactor toward a plugin-based static site generator that is a clear net improvement, but the mechanical convention score (0.52, 42 violations) sits below what the visible code suggests — the cited violations (e.g., class SsgEngine 'should be PascalCase') contradict the diff and point to analyzer/standard mismatch, so the low convention score should be validated against the repo's actual lint config rather than taken at face value.

problems.description: Cognitive complexity jumps +43 — all cache/hash/file-I/O logic is inlined into SsgEngine (loadCache, selectPagesToBuild, templateHash, fileExists, writeCache) rather than a dedicated cache module; the class now owns hashing, persistence, and build scheduling.
Cache file is derived as path.join(dirname(outputDir), '.ssg-cache.json'), coupling cache location to the output dir's parent rather than a configured/explicit path.
lastBuildStats is a public mutable field on the engine, leaking stateful build results between build() invocations.
Stale cache entries are never pruned: if a page is removed from content, its entry persists in the cache forever with no cleanup.

Flagged discrepancy: the 42 convention violations (PascalCase classes, UPPER_CASE constants, snake_case functions) cite cli.ts/config.ts/generator.ts, but config.ts is untouched by this diff and the diff itself uses camelCase functions and PascalCase classes — the low 0.52 score appears largely pre-existing analyzer noise rather than introduced here.
No tests in the diff covering cache read/write, skip-vs-rebuild selection, --clean forcing a full build, or template-change invalidation.

strengths: Integrates with the existing plugin lifecycle correctly — loadCache runs before onStart, writeCache after afterBuild — respecting the context/hook architecture.
Combines per-page source hash with a template-dir hash, a sound invalidation strategy that catches template-only edits.
Graceful ENOENT handling and a --clean override give sensible failure modes; CLI stats output is user-friendly and computed, not fabricated.
commit_reviews.summary: Solidly integrated incremental-build feature with a good invalidation strategy, but ships a +43 cognitive-complexity bump from monolithing cache logic into the engine and a low convention score that appears largely pre-existing.

compounding_issues: Session 1 greenfield-replaced the seeded baseline instead of building within its seams, destroying the domain-relevant structure (models/routes/error-handling) and forcing every later session to compensate

The monolithic generator.ts became the system's center of gravity: Session 5 re-monolithized incremental-cache logic into the engine (+43 complexity) even after Session 4's plugin refactor, and Session 3's server reused the same pipeline with only partial cleanup
Convention adherence locked in at ~0.52 across all five sessions; the naming/style choices made in Session 1 were never corrected
Session 1 shipped zero tests, creating persistent coverage debt that later sessions only partially repaid (live-reload and MIME paths left untested)
key_decisions: Greenfield replacement of the baseline seed with a fresh static-site-generator scaffold (Session 1)
Dev server integrated into the same generator pipeline with rebuild debouncing and a traversal guard rather than as a standalone process (Session 3)
Plugin/hook architecture (onStart/beforeBuild/afterBuild/onFile/onEnd) with per-concern plugins — markdown, template, dev-server — extracted from the monolith (Session 4)
Config-file-driven plugin loading via ssg.config.ts compiled with tsx (Session 4)
Content-hash-based incremental builds with a persisted render cache for skip-if-unchanged (Session 5)
story_review.trajectory_description: The arc is a classic 'rocky start, steady recovery' trajectory. Session 1 opened poorly — architectural fit 0.4, wholesale deletion of the baseline, a monolithic untested generator — then quality climbed through Session 2 (features plus first real tests, fit 0.85) and Session 3 (solid dev-server integration), reached its structural peak in Session 4's refactor into a clean plugin architecture (fit 0.85, larger removals than additions), and settled flat in Session 5, which delivered the cross-cutting incremental-build feature but at a measurable cognitive-complexity cost and a dip in fit to 0.68. Overall the codebase improved and matured substantially, but the early decisions constrained the ceiling.
story_review.summary: A logically coherent, improving five-session arc that overcame a weak greenfield start through a strong mid-project plugin refactor, though Session 1's monolith-and-testing decisions capped the final quality.
